newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to reduce military service to one year.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to reduce military service to one year.

text.p: Bulgaria will reduce its compulsory military service from 18 months to one year from January 1, Defence Minister Georgi Ananiev said on Wednesday.
Ananiev said the Supreme Military Council had approved a set of amendments to the Defence and Armed Forces Law for presentation to the government and parliament.

"With the proposed draft our aim is to lay the foundations for harmonising Bulgaria's legal system with European countries...to start structural reform in the Bulgarian army and set the legal grounds for a professional army," Ananiev told a news conference.

He said the reduction would cut army entrants by up to 15,000 every year, saving several billion levs from a tight military budget. Bulgaria has slashed government spending as part of IMF-prescribed reforms.
Armed Forces Chief of Staff General Miho Mihov said on Monday he wanted to modernise the army and improve its rapid reaction capability, but officers were struggling simply to keep conscripts fed.
The draft law also envisages a reduction of military service for university graduates to nine months from 12.
The reduction is expected to be approved by parliament in September so that it will be in force from January 1.
In 1990, the country's first multi-party parliament after four decades of communist rule cut six months off a two-year military service compulsory for all 18-year-old men.
